(Z)ero (D)ose Rate

Source: R/zd_rate.R
zd_rate.Rd

This function computes the proportion of people that have no record of receiving a given set of vaccines using data from the electronic immunization registry (EIR).

Usage

zd_rate(
  data.EIR,
  geo_level = "ADM0",
  vaccines = NULL,
  birth_cohorts = NULL,
  data.pop = NULL,
  data.pop_ids = NULL,
  fix_residence = TRUE
)

Arguments

data.EIR

Data frame. A data frame containing individual vaccination records. See immunABC.EIR for expected structure.

geo_level

Character. The geographic level to aggregate results by. Must be "ADM0", "ADM1" or "ADM2". If not specified, the default is "ADM0". Note also that if data.pop is in use, it must contain the columns to match.

vaccines

Character (optional). A character vector specifying the doses to include in the analysis. If NULL (default), all vaccines in data.EIR are included.

birth_cohorts

Numeric (optional). A vector specifying the birth cohort(s) for which the zero-dose rate should be calculated. If NULL (default), every person is included regardless of birth year. With data.pop, this also means every year in the population table; years with no records in data.EIR will show a zero-dose rate of 100.

data.pop

Data frame (optional). A data frame with population denominators. See immunABC.pop.ADMX for structure examples. If NULL (default) and no data.pop_ids is provided, the denominator is computed from data.EIR.

data.pop_ids

Data frame (optional). A data frame with individual population records (such as a civil registry) that can be cross-referenced with the EIR. See immunABC.pop_ids for expected structure. If provided, denominators are computed from it instead of data.pop or data.EIR. Its residence is never modified: when geo_level is "ADM1" or "ADM2", a warning reports the people whose residence differs from their residence in data.EIR, which should be corrected before running the analysis.

fix_residence

Logical. This function requires each person in data.EIR to have a single place of residence across all their vaccinations when geo_level is "ADM1" or "ADM2", so that each person is counted in a single area. When a person has more than one residence, TRUE (default) sets all their records to the residence of their most recent vaccination, and FALSE stops with an error.

Value

A data frame containing the zero-dose rate for each of the vaccines, birth cohort and geographic area, including groups where nobody was vaccinated. When vaccines is NULL, it also contains rows with dose "All", counting as vaccinated the people with at least one vaccine. A warning is raised when a group has more vaccinated people than population (negative zd_rate). To list each person and their vaccines, see zd_list.
